findings.issue: A cancelled part-read document is recorded as fully read. OcrService.Read catches OperationCanceledException and returns OcrState.Cancelled WITH the pages it had already read; ReadCoreAsync (line ~290) then branches only on `result.Pages.Count > 0` and calls SavePagesAsync, and SavePagesAsync (DocumentService.cs:621) unconditionally sets `document.OcrStatus = pages.Count > 0 ? OcrStatus.Done : OcrStatus.Failed` plus `PageCount = pages.Count`. So a twenty-page scan whose drain was cancelled on sign-out or shutdown after page 3 is stored as Done with PageCount 3; ResumeAsync only re-queues Pending/Running rows, so the remaining seventeen pages are never read and the document is silently half-indexed for B3-3 search. This is the one path the resume design exists for and no test covers it (A_run_cut_off_in_the_middle_is_picked_up_again_after_a_restart fakes the cut-off by writing OcrStatus.Running by hand, never by cancelling a read).
findings.fix: In OcrQueue.ReadCoreAsync, after `await _documents.SavePagesAsync(documentId, result.Pages, OcrLang, cancellationToken)`, add `if (result.State == OcrState.Cancelled) { await _documents.SetOcrStatusAsync(documentId, OcrStatus.Pending, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false); }` so the partial pages are kept but the document stays in line, and add a test that cancels a token mid-document (a fake engine that reports page 1 then honours the token) and asserts OcrStatus.Pending plus the partial pages, and that a fresh queue's ResumeAsync picks it up.

findings.issue: Line 747 writes the audit line with `actor: "system"`. Every other audited service in Core (CorrespondenceService.LogAsync/ActorAsync line 757-774, CorrectionService line 190) reads the installation's EmployeeName and passes it as the actor; a grep over src/Wakeel.Core shows this is the only literal actor in the whole layer. The result is that every «أُضيف الملف …» line in the immutable audit log names «system» instead of the person who added the file, so the log cannot answer who attached a document — and the inconsistency will show up in the admin tool's audit view beside correspondence lines that do name the account.
findings.fix: Mirror CorrespondenceService: add a `private string? _actor;` and a `private async Task<string> ActorAsync(CancellationToken ct) => _actor ??= await _db.Installation.AsNoTracking().Select(i => i.EmployeeName).FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct).ConfigureAwait(false) ?? string.Empty;`, and pass `await ActorAsync(cancellationToken)` instead of "system" in StoreAsync. Assert in DocumentServiceTests that the audit row for an import carries the seeded installation's employee name.

findings.issue: ScanAsync (line 296) short-circuits on `_scanner is null || !_scanner.IsAvailable`, but WiaScanner.IsAvailable is a cached field `_sawScanner` that starts false and is only set by ListDevicesAsync or by a scan that got as far as enumerating (WiaScanner.cs:71,79,187). A caller that asks to scan before it has asked for the device list therefore gets the «لا ماسح ضوئي» state on a machine that does have a scanner — a false negative in exactly the state the spec asks to get right. It cannot be caught here (no hardware) and it makes a cross-package call order load-bearing without saying so in IDocumentService's contract.
findings.fix: Drop the `|| !_scanner.IsAvailable` half of the guard in DocumentService.ScanAsync and let the scanner answer for itself: WiaScanner.Scan already returns ScanResult.NoScanner when CreateDeviceManager/DeviceInfos/FindDevice come back empty (and sets _sawScanner on the way), and DocumentService's existing `scan.Pages.Count == 0` branch already maps ScanState.NoScanner to CoreAr.Documents.NoScannerMessage. The existing test Without_a_scanner_the_answer_is_words_and_not_a_failure still passes, because FakeScanner.ScanAsync returns ScanResult.NoScanner when IsAvailable is false.

findings.issue: FindDevice (lines 416-457) releases `info` only on the fall-through path at line 453; both `continue` statements (line 428 for a null info — harmless — and line 434 when IsScanner is false) skip it, so every non-scanner WIA device enumerated during a scan leaks its COM wrapper. The class's own remark says a leaked device object leaves the hardware busy for the rest of the session.
findings.fix: Wrap the loop body in try/finally with `Release(info)` in the finally, releasing only when the method is not returning that object (e.g. set a local `var keep = false;` before `return info;` and release in the finally when `!keep`), as ListDevices already does.

findings.issue: Fingerprint (line 67-87) hashes only the file NAMES and LENGTHS of ara/eng.traineddata. Two different tessdata_best/tessdata_fast builds of the same language are routinely different files; if a replacement happens to have the same byte length, ReprocessChangedModelAsync (AGREEMENT item 30) will not notice and the documents keep text nobody can reproduce. The test The_model_fingerprint_changes_when_the_files_change only changes the length, so it does not exercise this.
findings.fix: Fold LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks into the joined string (`info.Name + ":" + info.Length + ":" + info.LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks`), or hash the first and last 64 KiB of each file; either keeps the call cheap and makes a same-size swap visible.

findings.issue: The third candidate (lines 104-110) walks up eight levels from AppContext.BaseDirectory yielding `<parent>\tools\tessdata`. That is what lets the tests find the repository copy, but it also runs in the shipped product: an installation under C:\Program Files\Wakeel\ would happily load model files from C:\Program Files\tools\tessdata or C:\tools\tessdata — a folder an unprivileged process can create on many machines — which is an unsigned input to the reader on a product that otherwise keeps everything under the installation.
findings.fix: Guard the walk-up candidate with a repository marker: only yield `<dir>\tools\tessdata` when `File.Exists(Path.Combine(dir.FullName, "Wakeel.slnx"))`, so a developer tree and the tests still find it and an installed product never does.

findings.issue: Combine (line 36) skips every sheet Skia cannot decode. When ALL of them fail it still closes the SKDocument and returns the bytes of a PDF with zero pages, which DocumentService.ScanAsync then stores as «مسح-….pdf» — a document the office can see, cannot open and whose OCR settles on Failed. The empty-input case throws, but the all-undecodable case does not.
findings.fix: Count the pages actually written and, when the count is 0, throw the same ArgumentException the empty list throws (or return an empty array and have DocumentService.ScanAsync fall through to its no-binder branch and store the sheets as separate images). Add a test with two undecodable sheets.

findings.issue: `_done` (lines 179, 211) and `_total` (lines 111, 206) are mutated outside `_gate`, which guards `_waiting` and Ordered(). ReadNowAsync called from a screen while DrainAsync is running on the thread pool — which is precisely the design (W45 reads one document now while the background batch drains) — can lose an increment and leave Progress.Done/Total disagreeing with reality, so the «اكتملت قراءة نصوص المستندات» sentence can appear early or never.
findings.fix: Move both increments inside `lock (_gate)` (or make them Interlocked.Increment) and read the pair under the lock inside Report.

findings.issue: The XML doc of IDocumentService.ScanAsync (lines 47-52) is garbled: «A machine with no scanner answers <see cref="DocumentImportState.KindNotAccepted"/>-free — it answers with the «لا ماسح ضوئي» sentence». It reads as a half-finished edit and cross-references the wrong enum member, which is the doc the screen package will read when wiring W45.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: «A machine with no scanner stores nothing and answers with the «لا ماسح ضوئي» sentence, so the dialog's other two ways in stay open.»

missing_spec_items: Nothing in the product ever starts the queue: a repo-wide grep finds no caller of IOcrQueue.ResumeAsync or DrainAsync outside tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests. Resume and drain are implemented and well tested, but as shipped today every imported picture/PDF stays at OcrStatus.Pending for ever and no page text is ever produced. Starting the resume on session open and the drain on an idle pass is arguably the shell's work and sits outside this package's 'App.xaml.cs DI lines only' allowance — it needs to be assigned explicitly to B3-2b rather than assumed.
notes:
COMMAND RUN EXACTLY AS GIVEN, ALL GREEN. dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core (0 warnings, 0 errors), src/Wakeel.Ocr (0/0), src/Wakeel.Desktop (0/0), tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests --no-dependencies (0/0); dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests --no-build: 675 passed, 1 skipped (the pre-existing Word skip), 676 total; tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests: 340 passed, 0 skipped; tests/Wakeel.Walkthrough.Tests: 20 passed. Zero warnings anywhere, so TreatWarningsAsErrors is genuinely clean and the two CA1416 suppressions in PdfRasterizer are the only ones, scoped to the two call sites with the reason written down.

WHAT I VERIFIED RATHER THAN TOOK ON TRUST.
- Vault crypto. Wakeel.Crypto/Primitives/Aead.cs is AES-GCM (AesGcm with a 16-byte tag) in framed chunks; VaultStore derives a per-file key with Hkdf.DeriveKey(vaultKey, Aead.KeySize, salt = the file's SHA-256 bytes, label \"wakeel.vault.file\"), and every frame authenticates the hex hash as associated data. The write is genuinely atomic (FileStream CreateNew to target + \".\" + GUID + \".tmp\", Flush(flushToDisk: true), File.Move(overwrite: false), temporary deleted on every failure path) and the IOException-when-target-exists race resolves to AlreadyStored. Reads verify twice: the AEAD tag per frame and an incremental SHA-256 of the plaintext against the name the file is filed under; VaultStoreTests proves tamper, truncation, a file moved to another hash's name, a wrong key, and dedup-does-not-rewrite (same mtime and length, one .bin under the whole vault). The vault key is fetched per call and CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory'd in a finally in both WriteCore and CopyToCore, and the desktop's SessionVaultKeyProvider keeps no copy, so locking the session really does take it away.
- No clear-text on disk. PdfRasterizer renders through PDFtoImage into PNG bytes in memory and OcrService hands them to Pix.LoadFromMemory; nothing anywhere writes an original outside the sealed .bin. The only caveat, correctly documented on VaultCopyResult, is that CopyToAsync streams plaintext into the caller's destination BEFORE the final hash check can fail, so a caller writing to a file must discard on a non-Ok state — DocumentService's own callers all pass MemoryStream or a sink.
- The move of VaultStore. src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/VaultStore.cs is deleted, ActivationService uses the static Core form (lines 261 and 435), and a grep shows no other reference anywhere. UI.Tests and Walkthrough.Tests are green; the two modified files under tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests are another package's live W07 recovery work and I left them alone.
- OCR on real pixels. The [OcrFact] tests RAN here (tools/tessdata is present): a generated PNG yields «Ministry»/«Report» exactly, Arabic letters with boxes, Arabic-Indic digits folded to western, and a generated two-page SKDocument PDF is rasterised and read page by page with per-page progress reporting Pages = 2. The skip attribute names build/get-models.ps1 and also checks for an Arabic-capable font, so a skip says something true. ScanPdfWriterTests is a real round trip (three drawn sheets in, PageCount 3 out, every page re-rendered as a PNG), not a stub.
- Limits and type safety. 20 MB is enforced from FileInfo.Length before the file is read in ImportFileAsync, and exactly 20 MB is allowed (asserted). A file is accepted only when FromFileName and Sniff agree, so a PNG renamed .pdf is refused (asserted), and .exe/.xlsx/no-extension are refused. Dedup is at both levels and the document row is deliberately saved before its link because document_links has an FK and no navigation; links revive with IgnoreQueryFilters because the unique index counts soft-deleted rows. I checked 0001_initial.sql: ix_documents_sha256 is NOT unique, so the one case the dedup lookup cannot see — a soft-deleted document with the same hash — creates a second row rather than violating a constraint. That is the right outcome and needs no change.
- Arabic. Every new sentence is a finished Arabic sentence with no code, no path and no library name; values that travel inside a sentence go through CoreAr.Isolate, and ScanPagesDone counts the way Arabic counts. Two tests assert western digits via ArabicOcrText.HasArabicIndicDigits. ArabicOcrText.Clean strips bidi controls and folds Arabic-Indic/Persian digits before anything is stored, which is what B3-3's indexer will need.
- DI. DocumentRegistrationTests assembles the desktop's container (ValidateScopes: true) and resolves IDocumentStore, IDocumentService, ILetterDocumentStore, IDerivedDocumentBuilder, IOcrEngine, IOcrQueue, IScanPdfWriter. WakeelPaths is a singleton in AddWakeelCore, so the singleton OcrService factory's GetService<WakeelPaths> is legal. The supervisor's two rulings are honoured: CoreAr is a static partial class with the documents strings in their own file, and B3-1b's two services are live.

ONE THING FOR THE NEXT PACKAGE, NOT A DEFECT HERE. OcrQueue is Scoped over the session's WakeelDb, which in the desktop is a single context shared with the Blazor UI. If B3-2b starts DrainAsync on a background task while a screen is querying, EF Core will throw its \"second operation on this context\" error. The class's own remark anticipates this («the host starts the drain from its own idle pass»), but the contract should be stated where the shell will read it, or the queue should be given its own scope.

Verdict is 'fix' only because of the three medium findings; nothing here is a rewrite. The cancelled-run status (finding 1) is the one that changes behaviour in the field, and it is a four-line change plus a test."
